Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

whether conjunction

in an indirect question

also if (= whether), to see if, to see whether

classical

Cato Agr. 2.1: satisne temperī opera sient cōnfecta, possitne quae reliqua sient cōnficere

-ne (+ subjunctive)

enclitic, on the first word of the question, with the subjunctive

An indirect question is a direct one put under a verb of asking, knowing or telling: the -ne stays and the verb goes into the subjunctive.

Other words

  • num (+ subjunctive) — whether

    conjunction, with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.59: quaerit ex proximō vīcīnō, num fēriae quaedam piscātōrum essent

    In an indirect question the same as -ne, without the “surely not” of a direct num.

  • sī — whether, to see if

    conjunction, after verbs of trying, waiting and looking · also used · classical · Petr. 33.2: temptēmus tamen, sī adhūc sorbilia sunt; Phaedr. 4.8.3–4: haec cum temptāret sī qua rēs esset cibī

    “To see whether”, after temptāre, experīrī, exspectāre, vidēre (Lewis & Short s.v. si).

  • an — whether (… not)

    conjunction, after verbs of doubting and not knowing · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.2.1: nec liquet mihi an dēbeam

    After dubitō, nesciō, haud sciō it leans towards yes: haud sciō an, I rather think.

Examples

  • vīlicum vocet, roget quid operis siet factum, quid restet, satisne temperī opera sient cōnfecta, possitne quae reliqua sient cōnficere

    let him call the overseer and ask what work has been done, what is left, whether the jobs were finished in time, whether he can finish what remainsCato Agr. 2.1

  • quaerit ex proximō vīcīnō, num fēriae quaedam piscātōrum essent, quod eōs nūllōs vidēret

    he asks the nearest neighbour whether it was some fishermen’s holiday, since he saw none of themCic. Off. 3.59

  • timeō nē jam conceptī sint. temptēmus tamen, sī adhūc sorbilia sunt

    I’m afraid they have chicks in them already. Let’s try, though, whether they can still be suckedPetr. 33.2

  • īrāscor, nec liquet mihi an dēbeam, sed īrāscor

    I am angry, and I am not sure whether I ought to be, but I am angryPlin. Ep. 2.2.1

See also whether … or, if, ask.
